title: Vincent van Gogh's birth chart
metaDescription: Vincent van Gogh's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 9.7° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 9.7° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 9.7° Aries — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mars. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aries and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — a trine, 1.4° wide. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Mars square Jupiter at 1.9°, and Venus conjunction Mars at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aries at 9.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Pisces at 28.1° is in exaltation; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 24.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 fire, 3 water, 3 earth; by modality, 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Every body was moving forward that day — no apparent reversals anywhere in the chart.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.2° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 21.3°.
